item.meaning: The market price at which the quantity demanded by buyers exactly equals the quantity supplied by sellers.

item.term: Minimum Support Price (MSP) & Maximum Retail Price (MRP)
item.meaning: MSP is a guaranteed government price floor for crops; MRP is the upper price limit legally chargeable to consumers.

item.definition: Any physical or virtual arrangement where buyers and sellers meet to exchange goods and services at agreed prices.

item.concept_name: Price Determination through Demand and Supply
item.description: Market equilibrium price is set where consumer demand curves intersect seller supply curves, balancing shortages and surpluses.

item.fact: Surat in Gujarat is Asia's largest synthetic textile hub and polishes over 90% of the world's diamonds, employing 1.5 million artisans.

item.geographical_historical_significance: Historic port and modern industrial textile/diamond hub located on the Tapi River.

item.institution_name: FSSAI (Food Safety and Standards Authority of India)
item.role_function: Regulatory body certifying food hygiene, safety standards, and mandatory product packaging licenses.

item.key_provisions: Ancient market regulation in the 'Arthashastra' requiring ghee sellers to give 1/50th extra quantity to compensate for liquid sticking to measuring cans.

item.cause: Extreme seasonal crop harvest surplus (e.g., tomatoes in Andhra Pradesh)
item.effect: Drives open market prices down to crash levels (e.g. ₹1/kg), requiring state Minimum Support Price (MSP) and cold storage interventions.

item.significance: The sequential flow of goods from raw farmers/manufacturers through wholesalers, distributors, and retailers to final consumers.
Regulatory price floors (MSP) protecting producers from price crashes and price ceilings (MRP) protecting consumers from gouging.
